solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Risk including what's central to source

parts.note: inc. is the standard abbreviation for including

indicators.note: what is central to a word is its middle, so only the core letters of the next word are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of source

explanation.surface: A warning that dipping into the heart of some source is a risky business.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a penalty is to run the risk of it, so the verbs are synonyms here.

clue.text: I've opinions — last of pair must be blown and brought low

indicators.note: something blown is lost or wasted, so that letter disappears from the phrase

parts.note: someone with opinions might say I'm biased
the phrase has two I's; the second is the one meant

explanation.surface: A confession of prejudice, then a pair of something blown and humbled.
explanation.walkthrough: I'M BIASED has two I's, a pair; the second is removed. Imbase is an old word for debase.
explanation.definitionFit: Imbased is an obsolete form of debased, meaning lowered in rank, worth or dignity.

clue.text: Like a story? Scottish island put up Irish outlaw

indicators.note: in a down entry, put up means written upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde
the original Tories were 17th-century Irish outlaws

explanation.surface: A tale in which a Hebridean island shelters a fugitive Irish bandit.
explanation.walkthrough: The political name Tory began as an insult meaning an Irish robber or outlaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Narratory means relating to narration, so having the nature of a told tale or story.

clue.text: Jug tending to block up

definitions.meaning: second meaning: liable to choke or clog

explanation.surface: A jug that keeps getting clogged.
explanation.walkthrough: Jug is old slang for prison, and so is choky, from Hindi chauki, a lock-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Choky is slang for a jail, and also an adjective for something liable to choke or obstruct.

clue.text: Billion lost in gross report by telephone

indicators.note: something lost is missing, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: to gross a sum is to bring in that much
B abbreviates billion

explanation.surface: A company that lost a billion phones in to report its gross takings.
explanation.walkthrough: B goes from BRING IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring in is to call one's workplace or a programme by phone to pass on news or a report.

clue.text: By the grace of God I'll be in band becoming wrinkly

indicators.note: something said to be in another thing sits inside it, so these letters go within the next word's

parts.note: a ring is a band, as on a finger
DG abbreviates Dei gratia, Latin for by the grace of God, as on British coins
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone vows that, God willing, they will join a band as they grow old and wrinkled.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin abbreviation appears on British coins after the monarch's name; it and the I go in together, not at the start of the band word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridging is forming ridges or furrows, as skin does when it wrinkles, so the participle matches.

clue.text: I read Greene madly as Magdalenian?

indicators.note: madly means wildly, without order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone devoured Graham Greene's novels wildly, like a reader of Mary Magdalene's era.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magdalenian is a late Palaeolithic culture named after La Madeleine in France, not Mary Magdalene.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reindeer Age is another name for the Magdalenian period, when reindeer were hunted heavily in Europe.

clue.text: One should try to ___ diet delivered around south

indicators.note: one word placed around another encloses it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: cards are dealt, that is delivered
S abbreviates south

explanation.surface: Health advice: cut the salt in the food that has been delivered to you.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank is a fill-in definition: the answer is the word that completes the advice.
explanation.definitionFit: To desalt is to remove salt, which health advice tells one to cut from one's food.

clue.text: Ditch one on film set

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small trench or drain, a dialect sense
second meaning: a stagehand who moves equipment on a film shoot

explanation.surface: Drop someone working on a movie shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A grip is both a small ditch or drain in Chambers and a crew member who handles film-set equipment.

clue.text: Swimmer circling without sloth

indicators.note: circling goes round something, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish
less can mean without, as in less the fee

explanation.surface: Someone in the pool laps round without any laziness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' in crosswords is often a fish, here a small European freshwater one.
explanation.definitionFit: Idlesse is a poetic word for idleness, the same vice as sloth or laziness.

clue.text: Ploughman Poet's neat nobility in need of Queen

indicators.note: something in need of a thing lacks it, so that letter is missing

parts.note: the gentry are the class just below the nobility
R is for Regina, queen

explanation.surface: Robert Burns's tidy aristocracy wants a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Burns was called the Ploughman Poet, so his word is Scots. R is removed from GENTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Genty is a Scots adjective, used by Burns, for neat, trim or elegant.

clue.text: Led up 'ere I prepared to wait before jumping

indicators.note: something prepared has been made ready or worked up, so these letters are rearranged into new order

parts.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A dialect speaker explains being led up here ready to wait before leaping into action.
explanation.walkthrough: Lie perdu or perdue is a Chambers phrase from French perdu, lost: to lie hidden in ambush.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie perdue is to lie concealed in ambush, waiting for the moment to spring out on someone.

clue.text: Such points interest NASA — for each is, on Earth, oddly alien

parts.note: per means for each

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the following word's letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
E abbreviates Earth; in a down entry what is on it comes above
five letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Lunar orbit points interest NASA because each, seen from Earth, looks strangely extraterrestrial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like a selector for odd letters, but here it scrambles alien. The definition is a loose phrase: points that interest a space agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Periselenia are the points of an orbit closest to the Moon, which matter to space agencies such as NASA.

clue.text: Benevolent helper to confess stuffing cheese

indicators.note: stuffing goes inside something, so this word's letters are packed within the other

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
to own up is to confess

explanation.surface: A kindly assistant admits to having filled up on cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore a brownie is a helpful household sprite that does chores at night, a kindly domestic spirit.

clue.text: Elderly nymph-chaser keeping it zipped for the most part

indicators.note: only most of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: someone keeping it zipped says nothing at all

explanation.surface: An old lecher pursuing nymphs mostly keeps his mouth shut about it.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth a silen or silenus is an old satyr-like woodland spirit, drunken companion of Dionysus and pursuer of nymphs.
explanation.definitionFit: Silens were elderly satyrs of Greek myth, famed for lechery towards nymphs in the woods.

clue.text: Barrels out of boat's boxes

indicators.note: something taken out of a word is removed from it, leaving the rest

parts.note: a bark or barque is a sailing boat; the possessive reads as a plural
B abbreviates barrels, as in bbl

explanation.surface: Barrels are unloaded from the boat's storage boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: The B is removed from BARKS. An ark in Chambers is also a chest or coffer, besides Noah's vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An ark is an old word for a chest or coffer, as in the Ark of the Covenant, so arks are boxes.

clue.text: Term for person in new military form of descent

indicators.note: new suggests made over afresh, so all the letters take a fresh arrangement
a term is an end or limit, so only the closing letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of person
eight letters to rearrange, with the added letter inside

explanation.surface: A word for someone serving in a newly formed army, as a kind of lineage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Term' looks like a word or name; it means the end, so only the last letter of person goes into the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Matriliny is tracing kinship and inheritance through the mother's line, a system of lineage.

clue.text: Audibly too wise to interrupt already-named follower of Fatima

indicators.note: something interrupting another thing breaks into its middle, so it goes inside

parts.note: the aforesaid is something already named

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the phrase is replaced by letters that sound like it

parts.note: spoken, too wise is two of the letter Y

explanation.surface: Someone excessively learned butts in on a previously mentioned devotee of the Prophet's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Fatima was the daughter of Muhammad; 'too wise' is said as two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sayyid is a title for a descendant of Muhammad through his daughter Fatima, hence her follower in lineage.

clue.text: Ailing state? Indubitably

parts.note: ailing means unwell
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A doctor asks whether someone is in poor health, and the answer is certainly yes.
explanation.definitionFit: I'll say is an emphatic exclamation of agreement, meaning certainly or without doubt.

clue.text: Agreeable air is in motor

parts.note: toon is a Scots spelling of tune, an air

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so these letters go within the car word

parts.note: an estate is a type of car, a motor
the 's contraction of is

explanation.surface: A pleasant melody plays inside the car.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British term for a station wagon; toon is the Scots spelling of tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Something to one's taste is pleasing and suits one's liking, so the phrase means agreeable.

clue.text: A killer? Och aye, mostly current during prohibition

indicators.note: something happening during another sits within its span, so it goes inside
mostly means not entirely, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ou ay is a Scots form of oh yes, like och aye
a ban is a prohibition
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A Scot confirms a murderer, with power running throughout prohibition.
explanation.walkthrough: Ou ay is the Scots exclamation, as in Chambers; only its last letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouabain is a deadly plant poison used on African arrow tips, so it is a killer.

clue.text: Government body edited software to manipulate data

parts.note: ed. abbreviates edited
Excel is Microsoft's spreadsheet software

explanation.surface: An official agency revised its spreadsheets to fiddle the figures.
explanation.walkthrough: Edexcel is a UK examination board, now privately owned by Pearson despite the clue's 'Government'.
explanation.definitionFit: Edexcel is a body that sets and awards school qualifications in Britain, such as GCSEs and A levels.

clue.text: Saw mistrust mostly by English needling pawnbroker?

indicators.note: a needle pierces into something, so the letter is pushed inside the other word
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to doubt is to mistrust
a pawnbroker lends money against goods
E abbreviates English

explanation.surface: Someone says they saw a distrust of pawnbrokers needling the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a past tense; it is the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-ender is anything with two working ends alike, such as a two-handled crosscut saw.

clue.text: Boat in loch near garden overlooking road

parts.note: L abbreviates loch or lake

indicators.note: overlooking can mean ignoring, so those letters are left out

parts.note: an orchard is a fruit garden
Rd abbreviates road

explanation.surface: A boat on a Scottish lake beside a garden above the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlooking' paints a view, but it means ignoring: RD is dropped from ORCHARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorcha is a light Chinese sailing vessel with a European-style hull and junk rig.

clue.text: Month in old French republic fixing drip in snout

indicators.note: fixing something in place sets it inside, so these letters go within the other word

parts.note: a snout is a nose
an IV is an intravenous drip

explanation.surface: Someone in the French revolutionary era fits a drip into a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Nivôse, the snowy month, was the fourth month of the French Revolutionary calendar, running from December to January.

clue.text: In spite of engaging, eg, Joplin tune crash as before

indicators.note: engaging can mean taking in or gripping, so one word holds the other

parts.note: for all that means in spite of it
Scott Joplin wrote ragtime, and a rag is such a tune

explanation.surface: Despite liking a Joplin piece, someone finds it all comes crashing down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' marks an obsolete word. Scott Joplin was the king of ragtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragor is an obsolete word, from Latin, for a loud crash or sudden noise.

clue.text: Following precedent of Romans these cannot be disputed

parts.note: f. abbreviates following, as in page references
the book of Acts comes just before Romans in the New Testament

explanation.surface: Legal precedents from Roman law are beyond argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precedent' suggests a legal ruling; it means what comes before.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts are things known to be true, so by nature they are beyond argument.

clue.text: Conductor wiping away last of cosmetic make-up

indicators.note: wiping away removes something, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a clippie was a bus conductor who clipped tickets

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of cosmetic

explanation.surface: A bus conductor wipes off the last of her cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: The C is taken from CLIPPIE. A clippie is British slang for a female bus conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Lippie is informal Australian and British slang for lipstick, a kind of make-up.

clue.text: Plot precisely hitting the mark over clubhouse

parts.note: pat means exactly right, as in off pat
CH abbreviates clubhouse

explanation.surface: A conspiracy aimed exactly at the club's building.
explanation.definitionFit: A patch is a small piece of ground, the same as a plot of land, as in a vegetable patch.

clue.text: Characterised by humour bordering on humility

parts.note: wit is humour

indicators.note: bordering on means at the edge of, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of humility

explanation.surface: A personality marked by humour close to modesty.
explanation.definitionFit: With can mean having or marked by, as in a man with patience, so it means characterised by.

clue.text: Mineral remains in cases with sound staff

parts.note: c/a, ca. is an abbreviation for cases in commerce
LX is theatre shorthand for the lighting and sound technical crew

explanation.surface: Some mineral is left over inside crates, along with the audio crew.
explanation.walkthrough: LX is backstage jargon for the electrics team. 'Sound' is not a sound-alike signal here; it describes the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Calx is the powdery residue left when a mineral or metal is strongly heated, so mineral remains.

clue.text: In Irish bars you'll get this cloudy pop cold

definitions.text: In Irish bars you'll get this

parts.note: c is the weather-map symbol for cloudy
rai is a style of Algerian pop music
C abbreviates cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: In Irish pubs you'll be served cloudy, cold fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Craic is Irish for fun, lively conversation and good times, the thing an Irish pub is famed for.

clue.text: Cigs not repackaged — that's shrewd

indicators.note: repackaged means put together in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Cigarettes not sold in new packs: a clever move.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnostic, from Greek for knowledge, can mean knowing or shrewd in Chambers, beyond its religious sense.

clue.text: I'm a believer in stock being reduced by bag

indicators.note: something reduced is cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a stock phrase is a trite one
to bag is to steal, and a heist is a robbery

explanation.surface: A convert declares faith in shares losing value through theft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm a believer in' seems to need an object; the solver reads only 'I'm a believer' as the answer speaking in the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: A tritheist believes in three gods, taking the Trinity as three separate deities: a believer of a sort.

clue.text: No longer pity husband according to language

parts.note: sin is an obsolete word for a pity, as in it's a sin
H abbreviates husband
à la means in the manner of, according to

explanation.surface: Someone stops feeling sorry for their husband, as the language has it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinhala is the language of the Sinhalese people of Sri Lanka, one of its official languages.

clue.text: They will unravel Latin compound

indicators.note: to unravel is to come undone, so the letters lose their order and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
L abbreviates Latin

explanation.surface: People predict a Latin compound will fall apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethyl is the chemical group C2H5, found in many organic compounds such as ethyl alcohol.
